long_biography.plain_text:
For nearly five decades, Riyadh's regional administration was the centre of Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud's public career. Born in the capital on 31 December 1935, he moved from municipal and regional leadership into national defence, then became crown prince before acceding as Saudi Arabia's king in 2015. This sequence, together with his birth date, distinguishes him from younger members of the extended dynasty who share parts of his name.

His profile is one of hereditary monarchy and public office, not a documented private commercial career. State institutions associated with the crown are legally and economically distinct from his personal property. No founder stake, operating company, private investment portfolio or inherited asset base is identified as the principal basis of his private wealth. Without such an asset, neither an industry nor an ownership relationship can be assigned.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative record gives December 1995, while every authoritative King Salman biography gives 31 December 1935. The exact name, title chronology, Saudi identity and Spain connection strongly resolve the record to King Salman, but the correction should be reviewed because it changes an existing immutable value.

A younger Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was born in November 1982 and has a longer lineage through Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman bin Mohammed. The authoritative record's December month, Spain residence and older Prince style fit King Salman instead; no reliable 1995-born exact namesake was found.

Prince was accurate before Salman's January 2015 accession and explains older records and Spanish government references. King is the current title and is proposed as a correction rather than treating the stale style as a different individual.

No reviewed source establishes a specific personally owned company, investment portfolio, trust interest or inherited private asset. Royal title, state leadership, public offices and dynastic membership are not substitutes for private ownership evidence.

Saudi government entities, state-owned companies, sovereign funds, public budgets, palaces used in office and other state assets are not attributed to Salman personally. No valuation of those assets is used for a personal wealth claim.

Forbes maintains an exact dedicated profile, but it is a power and public-office profile rather than a documented billionaire wealth profile. It verifies identity only and does not support a private net-worth or industry classification.
